clue.text: Note a leaning to become a Menshevik

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note
a list is a lean or tilt, as of a ship

explanation.surface: A musician's slight tilt somehow turns them into a Russian revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mensheviks were the moderate wing of Russian socialism that settled for minimum demands, hence the term.
explanation.definitionFit: Mensheviks were moderate socialists content with a minimum programme, so the label for one who seeks only modest change fits.

clue.text: Length determined by the number of feet

definitions.text: determined by the number of feet

explanation.surface: A measurement fixed by how many feet something has.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of length in the metric system; also poetic rhythm, set by how many feet each line has.

clue.text: I'm on top of the world

definitions.text: I'm on top of the world

parts.words: I'm on top of the world
parts.note: read literally, a place speaking of itself as the very topmost point of the globe rather than someone feeling elated

explanation.surface: A cheerful declaration of great happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern pole of the Earth's axis is at the top of the world on a conventional map.

clue.text: Tom. Dick or Harry — comic entertains them

indicators.note: something comic is played for laughs, so these letters are clowned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A comedian amuses ordinary people.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed full stop after Tom is an OCR slip for a comma: 'Tom, Dick or Harry' means anyone at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom, Dick or Harry stands for any ordinary person, the typical member of the public.

clue.text: Make much of one in the rugby side with energy

indicators.note: in places the word for one inside the rugby team's name

parts.note: the Lions are the British and Irish rugby touring side
one is the Roman numeral I
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Celebrate a player who gives his all for the rugby team.
explanation.walkthrough: The British and Irish LIONS are a rugby team picked from four home nations for overseas tours.
explanation.definitionFit: To lionise someone is to treat them as a celebrity and fuss over them.

clue.text: Run clogs up? With much pleasure

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: gums means clogs, as in gums up the works

indicators.note: much, not all, of the word so only most of its letters are kept

parts.note: glee is pleasure or delight

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether running in wooden shoes is a great pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses GUMS to SMUG; 'much' trims GLEE to GLE. 'Run' is the definition, as in run guns across a border.
explanation.definitionFit: To run contraband is to carry it illegally across a border, the trade of a smuggler.

clue.text: On a trip far from the equator

explanation.surface: Someone travelling well away from the tropics.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is intoxicated by drugs, on a trip; the other is high latitude, near a pole.

clue.text: Pig taking others' share

annotationWithheld.why: Pig taking others' share (5): Pig defines the answer (an ingot of metal), but no reading of 'taking others' share' builds IN+GOT or any other split of it; no blog or database parse found.

clue.text: People replace the point in weapon where the arms are kept

indicators.note: replace says one piece stands in for another within the weapon word

parts.note: a hatchet is a small axe used as a weapon
E, east, is a point of the compass
men means people

explanation.surface: Soldiers swap the tip of a weapon in an armoury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' is heraldic: a hatchment is a diamond-shaped board bearing a dead person's coat of arms, so 'where the arms are kept' is not an armoury.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchment is a funeral panel displaying the deceased's heraldic coat of arms.

clue.text: Train woman in race to come last

parts.note: to bring up a child is to train or rear it

indicators.note: in places the woman inside the race word

parts.note: tear means race or rush
her stands for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman training for a race finishes at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a noun or a railway but is the verb, as in rearing a child; 'race' means to rush, not a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up the rear is to come at the very back, in the final position.

clue.text: Fell upon city

parts.note: a fell is a hill, and a tor is a rocky hill
onto means upon

explanation.surface: Someone fell onto a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like a verb but is the noun for a hill, as in the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada.

clue.text: High-minded puritan drowned in a kind of milk

indicators.note: drowned in places the puritan wholly inside the milk

parts.note: UHT is ultra-heat-treated, long-life milk
a prig is a priggish puritan

explanation.surface: A moralising zealot is drowned in a vat of milk.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is honourable and principled, morally high-minded.

clue.text: Making improvements to inn, change original

indicators.note: original suggests something new and different, so these letters are newly arranged

explanation.surface: Renovating a pub by altering its first form.
explanation.definitionFit: Enhancing something means improving its quality or value.

clue.text: Starts in the nick of time calls 'Halt' in the nick

indicators.note: starts in means the opening letter of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: In the nick of time, someone calls 'Halt' at the police station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' is British slang for a police station; here the second one means a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a small cut or indentation, the same as a small V-shaped cut.

clue.text: The two are in the soup — right in

indicators.note: the final in tells us the right letter goes inside the word for the pair

parts.note: both means the two

explanation.surface: Two people are in trouble, right in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' is an idiom for being in trouble, so 'soup' hides as part of a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Broth is a thin soup of meat or vegetable stock.

clue.text: Distributing palms a bit of a sacrament

indicators.note: distributing spreads things out in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Handing out palm leaves is part of a church rite.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism is a Christian sacrament, and the adjective describes things belonging to it.

clue.text: Administrator gives flower to very attractive girl outside

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, and the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: outside puts the girl around the word for very

parts.note: a cutie is an attractive girl

explanation.surface: A manager sends flowers to a pretty woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword favourite: a thing that flows, a river. The Exe flows through Exeter in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An executive is a manager or official who administers an organisation.

clue.text: One grandmother and one wife are dead

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
nan is a familiar word for grandmother
one is the Roman numeral I
a mate is a spouse, here a wife

explanation.surface: A grandmother and a wife have both died.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inanimate is lifeless, without life.

clue.text: Shanghai journalists?

explanation.surface: Reporters in a Chinese city.
explanation.walkthrough: To shanghai someone is to force them into service at sea; the question mark flags the jokey reading of a gang of press reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: To shanghai means to force into naval service; also, whimsically, a group of reporters, the press.

clue.text: Annoyed, upset by drug

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone irritated and distressed by medication.
explanation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a painkilling drug.

clue.text: Entertained by first bit of gossip, wrote for another

indicators.note: first bit of means just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: hosted means entertained guests

explanation.surface: Someone amused by a morsel of gossip writes for someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostwriter writes material published under another person's name.

clue.text: Health food

explanation.surface: A wholesome diet.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast is a drink to someone's health; it is also grilled bread, a food.

clue.text: Bury is not wearisome at the start of the season

indicators.note: not says a letter is to be taken away from the season word

parts.note: winter is a season

indicators.note: at the start means only the opening letter of the word before is taken

explanation.surface: A Lancashire town is not tiresome at the beginning of the football season.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town in north-west England, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury a body in a grave.

clue.text: Understood the need to include "Island' in the address

indicators.note: to include means one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: address, in the sense of skill and diplomacy, means tact

explanation.surface: Someone recognises the need to mention an island in a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' means diplomatic skill, not a speech or a postal location.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means implied or understood without being spoken.

clue.text: Partisan set apart from the rest

explanation.surface: A biased supporter isolated from everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is biased, favouring a party; the other is aside, separated.

clue.text: Equally likely to win or lose a ball game, having dropped the first point

definitions.text: Equally likely to win or lose

indicators.note: having dropped the first tells us the opening letter goes from the game word

parts.note: sevens is seven-a-side rugby
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A ball game whose odds are even after an early point is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Sevens is a short form of rugby union played seven a side.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, odds of evens mean an even chance of winning or losing.

clue.text: Ridicule ass going round the Cape by rail

indicators.note: going round means the donkey word encircles the cape letter

parts.note: moke is British slang for a donkey
C abbreviates cape on maps
RY abbreviates railway

explanation.surface: A donkey travels around the Cape by train, to some mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: MOKE is British slang for a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Mockery is scornful ridicule or derision.

clue.text: Young English horse enters the driving area

indicators.note: enters says the English horse goes inside the golf term

parts.note: the tee is the golfer's area to drive from
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A young English horse comes onto the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenage describes someone adolescent, aged thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: Sealant in sack, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: loot is plunder, the spoils of sacking a town

explanation.surface: A sealant inside a sack, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: Lute is a clay or cement used to seal joints; it is not the instrument here.
explanation.definitionFit: Lute is a clay mixture used to seal joints and make them airtight.

clue.text: Small boat, when taken to loch, exhibits inclination to heel over under sail

definitions.text: inclination to heel over under sail

parts.note: a tender is a small boat serving a larger ship
Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A dinghy taken out on a Scottish lake tends to tip in the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender ship is one prone to heeling, so the quality describes the ship's lean under sail.
